categories.main_business_segments: CIJ operates primarily in the system development and related services sector, offering system design, manufacturing, operation, and maintenance. Its business includes system development, IT consulting and research, system/package integration services, and sales of computer products and related services. The company and its subsidiaries form a group focused on comprehensive IT solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company specializes in custom system development, leveraging advanced software engineering, project management, and integration of both proprietary and third-party software packages. It employs methodologies for both contract-based (waterfall/progress-based) and time-and-materials (dispatch/outsourcing) projects, with a growing emphasis on AI, DX (digital transformation), and cloud-based solutions. CIJ also invests in R&D for generative AI applications and workflow automation tools.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CIJ's key customers are large enterprises, particularly the NTT Group and Hitachi Group, which together account for nearly 40% of consolidated sales. The company serves a broad range of industries, including manufacturing, energy, public sector, finance, information, services, and telecommunications, with a notable presence in the energy and manufacturing sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Japan, with headquarters in Yokohama and major offices in Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, Sapporo, and Fukuoka. It also has an overseas subsidiary in the Philippines, but over 90% of sales and assets are concentrated in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: CIJ is positioned as a midstream IT services provider, acting as both a prime contractor and a subcontractor (SIer) for large-scale system development projects. It delivers end-to-end solutions, from consulting and design to integration and maintenance, often working closely with major system integrators and end-users.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include adapting to changing IT environments, expanding into new business domains, and developing specialized IT engineers (SEs). The company is investing in R&D for generative AI, digital transformation solutions, and standardized municipal information systems. Sustainability, human capital development, and expanding prime contract business are also key themes.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through contract-based system development, consulting, integration services, and maintenance, using both fixed-price and time-and-materials models. Additional income comes from software product sales and ongoing support services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CIJ competes with major Japanese IT service providers and system integrators such as SCSK, Fujitsu, NEC, and other mid-sized SIers. It differentiates itself through strong relationships with NTT and Hitachi, a focus on custom development, and a growing portfolio of proprietary solutions and AI-driven services.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending June 2025, CIJ reported consolidated sales of approximately 26.9 billion yen, with operating profit of 2.17 billion yen and net profit of 1.5 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth, with a 4.5% increase in sales and a 57.7% increase in net profit year-on-year, and targets further growth to 30 billion yen in sales by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CIJ emphasizes its ability to provide high-value, customized IT solutions and long-term partnerships with major clients. Its strengths include deep technical expertise, a track record in mission-critical systems, responsiveness to new technologies (AI, DX), and a commitment to sustainability and human capital development. The company positions itself as a trusted strategic IT partner capable of supporting clients' business expansion and transformation.
